week1.text: In the first 7 days we validated 9 attack paths and confirmed 2 closed, with a median of 4.5 days from validation to confirmed close. Of the 7 paths still open, 4 reach crown jewels, and Network Engineering owns 4 of the open paths, including both VPN routes to the domain controller. Teams acknowledged 8 tickets within 2 days across 6 teams, so owners are engaged and the remaining work is in fixing. The substation router path to the EMS data link is waiting on an OT change window scheduled for day 35, after this pilot ends, and we need your help securing an earlier window.

week4.text: By day 28 the pilot validated 12 attack paths and confirmed 10 closed, with a median of 6.0 days from validation to confirmed close and the slowest at 20 days. Teams responded well, acknowledging 11 tickets within 2 days across 8 teams. The 2 open paths both reach crown jewels via the EMS data link: a substation router path owned by Field Telecom, open 22 days, and a corporate-to-OT jump host path owned by OT Engineering, open 11 days. Both wait on an OT change window scheduled for day 35. This week, please approve an earlier OT change window or formally accept the risk until day 35.
